X.note: The buildings are strong: peeling plaster, shutters and balconies with good materials and haze. The figures are the problem. They are featureless olive-grey mannequins in uniform poses, many in a clump on the right, and several are semi-transparent or washed blue. They read as clay or game placeholders. There is no clear subject, and the shadow pools look blotchy on the cobbles.

Y.note: The same excellent set. The figures are more varied and read as intended: white-uniformed sailors with blue collars in the foreground, khaki troops and a dark-uniformed figure in the middle, and a small group around a central point. A sandbag stack at lower left adds wartime context. The people are still low-poly, stiff and small, with faceless blobs and a bright halo around the sailors. The group has some grouping and focus, but the scale and lighting integration are weak.

why: The environment is identical, but Y's costumed, grouped figures and the sandbag detail give a readable scene, while X's uniform grey mannequins look like unfinished placeholders.
top_fix_for_weaker: Replace the identical grey mannequins with a varied, properly textured and lit crowd (mixed 1943 naval whites, khaki battledress, civilians, different heights and poses). Remove the clumping and transparency, and add contact shadows and a focal action.
anachronisms_seen: Union Jack with no obvious issue (flag looks plausible for 1943)
Modern-looking clean lamp post and plain bollards at the quay edge (minor)
Generic mannequin figures with no period-specific clothing in X
Sailors' white uniforms in Y look more like a generic summer rig than wartime issue (minor)
